issues: Summary assigns speech to Lehi and says he is addressing his sons, but verse 2 only identifies the speaker as “my father” and the audience as “us”; the summary could be precise to those terms.

The narrator of 1 Nephi 8 is Lehi, not Nephi; the supplied verses say Lehi speaks of his dream, and the first-person narrator continues through verses 7–8. Labeling him Nephi and saying Nephi follows someone invents the speaker/actor.

The source says the man bade the narrator to follow him; it does not say the person remained unidentified in the scene as a distinct present character after that. The character listing risks implying continued presence, which the scene itself leaves unspecified.

The summary says he “begins to pray … for mercy,” while the verse reports a prayer seeking mercy, not direct spoken dialogue; this is acceptable as summary but the narrative presentation should preserve the reported-event framing.

The request's established-character convention supports labeling the first-person narrator as Nephi, but the supplied verses do not name the narrator in this passage; the character attribution is therefore an editorial inference.

The summary says the narrator sees Sariah, Sam, and Nephi standing at the river’s head, but the supplied verse does not establish the first-person narrator as Nephi. The character label and story note assert this identification using information outside the supplied verses.
The explicit fact that the narrator is Nephi likewise lacks support in the supplied source. The source itself names Nephi among those observed, but does not identify the narrator.

Lehi is not named within verses 17–18; the first-person observer can be carried forward from the preceding Lehi dream account, but the scene should mark that continuity as contextual rather than explicit within these verses.
The scene misidentifies the first-person observer as Nephi. The supplied verses continue Lehi’s account; it is Lehi who stands by the tree. Nephi is not shown in these verses.
The summary and explicit facts wrongly place Nephi at the tree and make him behold the rod and path.
Lehi is not named in verses 21–22; identifying the observer as Lehi relies on continuity from the preceding first-person dream account, not explicit naming in these verses.
Identifies the first-person observer as Nephi in the summary and character list, but verses 24–25 do not name the observer.
Identifies the first-person observer as Nephi in the summary and character list, but verses 26–27 do not name the observer.

Lehi is not named in verse 28. The events are accurately summarized, but identifying the narrator/observer as Lehi would rely on continuity beyond the verse; the scene correctly avoids that attribution.
